blocks.text: Zscaler Asset Exposure Management (AEM) allows organizations to collect and manage asset data from various sources to track and manage asset inventory and coverage. With AEM, you can create policies that ensure asset compliance across your organization's assets.

blocks.item: Ensuring your organization's Configuration Management Database (CMDB) contains a comprehensive and accurate inventory of assets.
Identifying and tracking tool coverage gaps.

blocks.text: Policy rules are designed to generate policy violations on assets that are out of compliance with a given security standard in your organization. Policy violations can then be assigned to a designated owner, tracked against a specific SLA deadline, and prioritized with a severity score. When assigned, these violations can be dispatched to relevant team members for prompt action. Automatically alerting you to policy violations helps organizations operationalize efforts to drive compliance with asset-related policies.

Creating new policies for tracking asset compliance involves selecting the policy category, defining the asset population that the policy applies to, and setting the policy scenario (i.e., the conditions that generate a policy violation).

For access to Policies, your assigned role must include the Read, Create, Edit permissions under the Assets App > Policy Rule resource. To learn more, see Creating Custom Roles and Assigning Roles to Users. The Asset Admin can create and manage policies, but can't delete them.

blocks.item: The Create New Policy page appears.
On the Create New Policy page, configure the following sections:
Click Preview to test and adjust the policy configuration. This displays the top 50 policy violations generated by the policy.

blocks.text: After creating and saving a policy, assets that violate the policy automatically generate policy violations, which can be viewed and monitored on the Policy Violations page. The policy violations are aggregated into violation tickets that can be tracked on the Violation Tickets page.
You can manage and adjust the policy's settings and criteria in the Policies table. To learn more, see Managing Asset Compliance Policies.
After creating the policy, save the policy to complete the process in one of the following ways:

blocks.item: Click Save to save the policy. The policy will apply the next time data is ingested into your account.
In the Save drop-down menu, click Save & Run to save the policy and immediately run it.
